ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Treating the underlying cause

A 42-year-old woman has a duodenal ulcer and confirmed active H. pylori infection. Her pain improves on a PPI. Which additional treatment goal is important to reduce the risk of ulcer recurrence rather than addressing acid alone?

  1. Use antibiotics only if diarrhea develops
  2. Stop all follow-up when pain disappears
  3. Replace eradication therapy with dietary spice avoidance alone
  4. Eradicate H. pylori and confirm cure
  5. Continue acid suppression but never treat the infection
Answer and explanation

Eradicate H. pylori and confirm cure

Treating the infection addresses an underlying cause of recurrent ulcer disease.

Option explanations

Eradicate H. pylori and confirm cure: Treating the infection addresses an underlying cause of recurrent ulcer disease.

Continue acid suppression but never treat the infection: Symptom control alone leaves the causal infection untreated.

Use antibiotics only if diarrhea develops: Diarrhea is not required for H. pylori eradication treatment.

Stop all follow-up when pain disappears: Symptoms do not prove eradication.

Replace eradication therapy with dietary spice avoidance alone: Dietary measures do not eradicate H. pylori.
